channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro, el ungido por el patriarca para reconquistar el poder
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, PL candidate for the 2026 Brazilian elections, is portrayed as the most moderate member of the Bolsonaro family but still carries the ideological legacy of his father, Jair Bolsonaro. Although he does not display the same radical rhetoric, his political agenda reflects the influence of the patriarch. As the most-voted candidate in the first round, he signals strong support for maintaining the Bolsonaro base in Brazil.

item.title: Lula, la batalla final
item.description: Lula emphasized his epic life trajectory at the UN, referencing his mother doña Lindu's influence on his character formation. In his tenth General Assembly speech, he addressed sovereignty and democracy while revisiting his grassroots origins in new rallies. The campaign evokes nostalgia from the past struggle against the dictatorship.

item.title: O vexame das pesquisas para Presidência da República em 2026
item.description: All major polling institutes miscalculated the first-round predictions for the 2026 Brazilian presidential election, with Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) leading at 47.21% of valid votes, compared to 44.95% for Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT). The runoff is confirmed, and the polls significantly diverged from the actual results.

item.title: Eleições: 11 governadores são reeleitos no 1º turno. 3 disputam o 2º turno
item.description: In the first round of the 2026 elections, 11 governors were re-elected, three will run in the second round, and five lost. Wins were concentrated in the Northeast and Southeast, highlight Tarcísio de Freitas (SP) and Jorginho Mello (SC).

item.title: Reeleito em SP, Tarcísio promete empenho para eleger Flávio
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas, re-elected governor of São Paulo, pledged to work toward electing Flávio Bolsonaro as president in 2026, criticizing President Lula's administration. He emphasized the need to unite forces to change the country's direction.

item.title: Caiado fica em 3º em Goiás, atrás de Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) secured 12.29% of valid votes in Goiás, placing third behind Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) and Lula (PT) in the state presidential election.

item.title: Carlos Portinho e Carlos Jordy são eleitos ao Senado pelo Rio
item.description: Carlos Portinho and Carlos Jordy, both from PL, were elected to the Senate for Rio de Janeiro with 26.78% and 24.57% of the votes respectively. Their victory ensures PL two seats in the state representation, maintaining the party's influence in the Senate. The race also underscored the Senate's importance for national political balance.

item.title: “Onde tiver PT, estaremos do outro lado”, diz Zema ao sinalizar apoio a Flávio
item.description: After failing to advance to the presidential runoff, Romeu Zema (Novo) signaled support for Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) if he faces Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) in the second round. Zema stated he, Eduardo Girão, and the Novo party will be on the opposite side of the PT. The statement reinforces ideological alignment among democrats against the PT.

item.title: Citados no caso Master vão bem nas urnas; mas Ciro Nogueira não se reelege
item.description: Parliament members linked to the Banco Master scandal performed well in the election. Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) advances to the second round and is flagged as intermediary in funding the film 'Dark Horse'. Ciro Nogueira is not re-elected.

item.title: Confira a lista completa de deputados federais eleitos em Mato Grosso do Sul
item.description: Over 2 million voters in Mato Grosso do Sul elected eight federal deputies to the Chamber of Deputies. The elected candidates represent parties such as PL, Republicans, PP, PT, and União, with notable wins including Marcos Pollon, Mara Caseiro, and Beto Pereira.

item.title: Allyson e Cadu de Lula vão ao 2º turno no Rio Grande do Norte
item.description: Allyson Bezerra (União Brasil) and Cadu de Lula (PT) moved on to the second round of the Rio Grande do Norte gubernatorial election, with 36.79% and 36.24% of the valid votes. Álvaro Dias (PL) placed third and was eliminated. The final vote will take place on October 25th, with the winner succeeding Fátima Bezerra (PT), who is ineligible for another term.

item.title: Campanha de Lula já fala em ir atrás de eleitores ausentes
item.description: Lula's campaign is already planning to target absent voters from the first round to reduce the gap against Flávio Bolsonaro in the second round. The team faces challenges in attracting right-wing votes, and Lula remained calm during the unfavorable initial results.

item.title: Nikolas Ferreira bate recorde e é reeleito deputado federal com o dobro dos votos de 2022
item.description: Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) was reelected federal deputy with over 3 million votes, more than double his 2022 tally. Known for viral videos and controversial stances, he aligned with Flávio Bolsonaro in the final weeks of the campaign and faces investigations into ties with businessman Daniel Vorcaro.

item.title: Lula repete feito contra Jair e ganha de Flávio na cidade de São Paulo
item.description: In the simulated election in São Paulo, Lula defeated Flávio Bolsonaro with 46.58% of the vote against 42.13%. In 2022, Lula also beat Jair Bolsonaro in the capital, reinforcing his strength in the region. However, Flávio led in the state of São Paulo with 51.93%.

item.title: Teresa Leitão diz que PT buscará novas alianças no 2º turno
item.description: Teresa Leitão states that the PT will seek new alliances in the second round, changing strategy and campaign teams. She highlights congressional debates, such as the Public Security PEC and the end of the 6X1 scale, as part of the campaign. The senator compares the strategy to the 2022 election and stresses that the second round requires a different approach.

item.title: Segundo turno entre Ruas e Paes no Rio agora depende do TSE; entenda que acontece com os votos de Garotinho
item.description: The runoff election in Rio de Janeiro between Douglas Ruas (PL) and Eduardo Paes (PSD) remains pending as the TSE reviews the appeal from Garotinho, whose votes are currently annulled sub judice.

item.title: Campanha de Lula faz reunião virtual após resultado do 1º turno
item.description: A faction of Lula's campaign held a virtual meeting after the first round results to assess the scenario and adjust strategy for the second round. Although there was an expectation that Lula would lead, the Ministry of Social Communication expressed concern about the electoral landscape. The campaign plans a new in-person meeting in Brasília to finalize second-round strategies.

item.title: Sucessor de Caiado, Daniel Vilela é reeleito governador de Goiás
item.description: Daniel Vilela (MDB) was reelected governor of Goiás with 59.17% of the votes, defeating Wilder Morais (PL), who received 21.96%. Vilela assumed office after Ronaldo Caiado left to run for president and represents continuity of the prior administration. Wilder's campaign was marked by controversies involving Bolsonarism and internal divisions within the state PL.

item.title: Omaz Aziz (PSD) e Professora Maria do Carmo (PL) vão ao 2º turno pelo governo do Amazonas
item.description: Omar Aziz (PSD) and Professor Maria do Carmo (PL) advanced to the runoff in the Amazonas gubernatorial election, securing 40.34% and 24.77% of the votes, respectively. Incumbent Governor Roberto Cidade (União Brasil) placed third with 21.80%, according to results with 98.05% of precincts reported.

item.title: Jerônimo vence ACM Neto com 55,26% dos votos e é reeleito governador da Bahia
item.description: Jerônimo Rodrigues (PT) was reelected governor of Bahia with 55.26% of the votes in the first round, defeating ACM Neto (União Brasil), who received 44.25%. The victory ends the election in the first round, something not seen since 2018, and keeps the PT in power in the state since 2007.

item.title: Zema comemora desempenho da direita e anuncia que estará contra o PT no segundo turno: 'Missão concluída'
item.description: Romeu Zema celebrated the right-wing advance in the 2026 elections and announced support for the PT in the second round, stating 'Mission accomplished' after the Novo party reached the electoral threshold. The campaign was marked by controversies, such as using a phone inside the voting booth.

item.title: Maioria dos presidiários da Papuda dá preferência a Lula
item.description: Provisional prisoners at polling station 0420 of the 18th Electoral Zone in Brasília voted in the election and showed preference for Lula (PT), who received 74 votes against 70 for Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). Results were recorded in the TSE poll book.
